resources.string: Hear Do / Re / Mi, and sing in tune
Follow system is the default: Chinese systems use Simplified Chinese; other languages use English. A manual choice is saved. Changing language stops current audio but keeps scores and settings.
Listen to the chord and Do to establish the key, then sing the requested solfege note. Wait for playback to finish.
Remember Do, then identify the last note as Do, Re, or Mi. Start with three notes and work up to all seven.
Movable Do follows the key, not a fixed C. Do stays the same within a round; a new round selects a new key.
Learn the sounds from the demo, then hear one short note per question
Listen to C4, then sing the note shown above
Hear the answer again, then continue
Select any C4–C5 natural notes. Only selected notes will be tested.
Keep at least one note selected.
An eighth note takes half a beat: %1$d ms per note, including a short silent gap. Tempo affects playback, not your answer deadline.
Tap white keys to hear Do–Do↑ (C4–C5). Scroll on narrow screens or expand to landscape fullscreen. Previews do not change your range or save a score.
The piano is separate from training and detection. Rapid taps switch short synthesized notes. Exit fullscreen with the button or Android Back.
Piano preview stopped. Tap a key to play again.
A fixed 10-second window shows notes or a pitch curve. Stop to review, replay or manually save the full clip, up to 3 minutes. This is not reliable complex-music transcription.
The display shows 10 seconds at a time; the complete clip is kept for up to 3 minutes.
Note timeline; the red cursor shows actual synthesized audio progress
No stable notes to replay yet. Listen to a clear single-note melody, then stop.
Fixed 10-second window · C4 = Do · Drag or use the slider to review after stopping.
%1$s timeline, showing %2$.1f to %3$.1f seconds; pitch references include chromatic notes
Up to 3 minutes per clip. The full clip is retained, not just the visible window. Backgrounding stops listening; an unsaved clip stays in memory until replaced or the app closes.
Reached the 3-minute limit. Listening stopped; review or save the complete clip.
Replay uses synthesized notes, not the original recording. Silence and note durations are preserved. Curves help inspect single-note melodies, not transcribe accompaniment or chords.
This clip has not been saved. Starting again will discard it. Cancel to review or save first.
One entry per manually saved clip. No score or accuracy is assigned. Stored locally: notes, downsampled pitch curve, timestamps and tuning; no original audio.
No saved clips yet. Stop listening and tap Save detection clip.
A4 = %1$.0f Hz · Curve-only clips may have no stable notes to replay.
Delete this detection clip and its pitch data? This cannot be undone.
Clip not found. Refresh local data and try again.
Cannot complete the clip operation: %1$s. Please retry; existing practice scores are unchanged.
Tap notes to match solfege, pitch names, and sounds. Do↑ is the higher Do at C5.
Decorative eighth note; no answer pitch is shown before answering
Choose a note in the selected training range.
Pitch error %1$+.0f cents; the center means in tune

One entry per practice; tap for per-note answers. The latest 100 practices are shown. Overall accuracy includes all answered questions, different ranges, and legacy modes; it is not a standardized ability level.
Practice not found. Refresh history and try again.
Cannot load practice details: %1$s. Retry or return to history.
Default A4 = 440 Hz; C4 is about 261.63 Hz. Changing A4 adjusts the tuning of both playback and detection.
New users must match the octave. Existing preferences are kept. Ignoring octaves affects singing only; listening still distinguishes C4 from C5.
Contacts GitHub Releases only when tapped, including published previews. No background checks or uploads of audio or scores.
Opens the APK link for a supported architecture, or the universal package if none matches. Install the download manually over an official version to keep your history.
Cannot check for updates. Check your connection and retry. Offline practice still works.
Release information or APK assets are incomplete. Try again later or open the releases page.
GitHub denied the request, possibly due to rate limits. Try again later or open the releases page.
Cannot open the link. Install or enable a browser and try again.
Demo order: establish Do, hear %1$s in sequence, then return to Do.
Round complete. You can start another.
Note outside the current major scale
Detect a single voice or instrument melody live. No song identification or reliable chord/accompaniment transcription.
Sing the target note (up to 8 seconds)
Timed out: no stable note. Check noise and distance, or try holding a steadier pitch.
Audio stopped. Unfinished questions do not count; you can continue practicing.
Microphone permission is needed for singing and detection. Listening practice still works. If permanently denied, enable it in Android app settings.
Audio unavailable: %1$s. Stop other recording apps and retry.
Playback format not supported by this device
The playback device did not finish output
Recording format not supported by this device
Local data operation failed: %1$s. Score saving is unconfirmed; please retry.
Ignore octave when singing (allow an octave above/below)
Training notes: C4–C5 natural notes. Detection covers about 65–1000 Hz.

Original audio is never saved or uploaded. Detection clips save only note events and a downsampled pitch curve when you tap Save. Practice history is separate; deleting practice scores does not delete clips. Backgrounding or leaving detection stops listening. Only a manual update check contacts GitHub.
Delete all practice scores? Detection clips and settings will be kept. This cannot be undone.
No practice history yet. Listening and singing answers are saved automatically.
Total %1$d questions, %2$d correct; latest 100 questions below.
Pitch curve over the latest 10 seconds; vertical axis is MIDI pitch
Start listening to show sustained single notes here. Leave short pauses between repeated notes.
Early preview: real-device validation is still needed. Not a professional musical-ability assessment.
